AI Productivity Coach

A coach for the gap between what you plan and what you actually do. It helps you choose what matters, break big tasks into small ones and design a day you can stick to.

TL;DR
  • Best for weekly planning, procrastination and protecting focus time.
  • Tell it your real schedule, energy levels and the task you keep avoiding.
  • Small plans you follow beat perfect plans you don't: ask for the smallest next step.

What this coach helps with

  • Planning a realistic week
  • Breaking a big project into small tasks
  • Getting started on a task you keep avoiding
  • Protecting time for deep work
  • Building a morning or evening routine

Prompts you can copy

Copy a prompt, paste it into the Zehn AI Chat or any AI assistant, and replace the parts in [brackets] with your own details.

  1. Act as my productivity coach. Here is everything on my mind: [brain dump]. Sort it into do today, this week, later and delete.

  2. I keep avoiding [task]. Ask me why, then break it into steps so small that the first one takes under 5 minutes.

  3. My week looks like this: [schedule]. Find two 90-minute blocks for deep work and tell me what to move to make room.

  4. I have the most energy at [time] and the least at [time]. Rearrange my day so hard work happens when I'm sharp.

  5. Design a 20-minute morning routine for someone who [situation, e.g. has small kids].

  6. I have [number] hours this week for [project]. Make a plan with a clear finish line for each session.

  7. Help me say no. Write a polite reply to [request] that protects my time without damaging the relationship.

  8. I lose time to [phone, email, meetings]. Suggest three rules I can test for one week and how to measure if they work.

  9. Run a weekly review with me: ask what went well, what slipped and what to change, one question at a time.

  10. Give me a shutdown routine for the end of the workday so I stop thinking about work in the evening.

  11. My to-do list has [number] items. Help me pick the three that would make the biggest difference by Friday.

  12. Be my accountability partner: I'll tell you my plan for today; tonight ask me what I finished and why the rest didn't happen.

Two example conversations

Written by the Intellect AI team to show the style of answers. Not a real user conversation.

ExampleStarting a report you keep postponing

YouI have to write a 10-page report and I've avoided it for a week.

Productivity CoachLet's make it smaller. For the next 10 minutes, only write the five headings, no sentences. Then pick the easiest heading and write three rough bullet points under it. Messy is fine. When the timer ends, tell me how it went and we'll plan the next block.

ExampleA week with too many meetings

YouI have 14 meetings this week and no time for actual work.

Productivity CoachGo through the list with one question: would anything break if I skipped this or sent notes instead? Most people can drop two or three. Then book two 90-minute focus blocks in your calendar before anyone else takes them. Which meetings are recurring?

Tips for better answers

  • Be honest about your energy, not just your hours. A plan that ignores tiredness fails by Wednesday.
  • Ask for the smallest possible first step whenever you feel stuck.
  • Use the coach for a weekly review every Friday; it's where most of the value is.
  • Fewer priorities work better: three a day is plenty.

Questions people ask

Can AI really help with procrastination?

It can help with the part that keeps you stuck: tasks that feel too big or too vague. A productivity coach breaks work into tiny steps, asks what you're avoiding and checks in on you. It cannot do the work for you, but starting is usually the hardest part, and that is where it helps most.

What is time blocking and should I use it?

Time blocking means reserving fixed slots in your calendar for specific work, like a meeting with yourself. It protects focus and makes your real capacity visible. It suits people with flexible schedules. Ask the coach to block one week with you and adjust after seeing what actually happened.

How should I start a chat with the productivity coach?

Start with a brain dump: everything on your mind, in any order. Add your fixed commitments and when you have the most energy. Then ask for a plan for today or this week. A short honest picture of your situation works better than a long list of goals.

Is an AI productivity coach useful for students?

Yes. Students use it to plan revision, split assignments into steps and build study routines around classes. It can quiz you on a schedule and help you start when motivation is low. It should not write your assignments; use it to organise the work, then do the thinking yourself.
